canonical_serialization.comparability_key: 'cmp--' + sha256('|'.join(str(key_inputs[f]) for f in comparability_key_field_order)).hexdigest()[:16]; inputs are enum values and ids, none of which may contain '|'
canonical_serialization.description: The single serialization rule used for every derived hash and every line in data/*.jsonl. registry_add.py and registry_validate.py both call tools/registry_lib.py, so they cannot drift.
canonical_serialization.floats: repr() of the IEEE-754 double; values are never rounded on the way in
canonical_serialization.jsonl: one canonical object per line, file sorted ascending by the record id
canonical_serialization.scope_digest_numbers: bits_per_weight renders as str(int(v)) when integral, else repr(float(v)), so 6 and 6.0 agree

description: JSON Schema enforces the shape of one record. These are the checks that need two or more records, or a recomputation. registry_validate.py must implement every id below and report failures with the invariant id. Severity 'error' fails the run; 'warn' is reported and does not fail unless --strict.

invariants.statement: estimator.stack_relation=cross_stack requires comparability.bias with kind=cross_stack_capture_replay, a non-unknown direction, and either floor_measurement_ref or an explicit detail saying no floor exists.
comparability.bias.floor_measurement_ref, when set, points at a measurement with the SAME comparability.key as the biased row. A floor from a different panel or estimator is not a floor.
A row with any bias block is never comparability.class=strict.

invariants.amended: v1.0.0: the cross-engine GGUF floor measures unsloth's BF16 .gguf repack of Qwen3.8-27B, not the reference safetensors themselves. Requiring literal artifact equality would have rejected a correct floor.
invariants.statement: comparability.bias.floor_measurement_ref points at a row measuring the reference's own artifact, or an artifact of kind=base that derives from it -- for a cross-ENGINE floor the unquantized weights are necessarily repackaged for the other engine (a BF16 .gguf of the same base). A floor measures unquantized weights through the candidate's stack; anything else is a comparison, not a floor.
A floor row (artifact_ref == the reference's artifact_ref) is reported so the renderer can label it 'measurement floor' rather than ranking it as a quantization result.

comparability.bias.floor_measurement_ref, when set, points at a measurement produced by a pipeline declaring the SAME measurement lane as the biased row's own pipeline (a pipeline with no `lane` object is the sealed-ep8 lane). The comparability key carries no lane input (PROV-012), so a sealed-lane row and a streaming-lane row of the same artifact routinely share one key, and BIAS-002's same-key check alone would let a floor measured on one lane be named as another lane's zero-point. A floor is the zero-point for its own lane only: this registry's cross-stack floor (0.012712 nats, pipeline--malaiwah.glm53-crosscheck) must never be subtracted from a streaming-lane row, nor a streaming-lane floor from a cross-stack row, even where the two rows happen to share a comparability key.

a row whose comparability.usable_as_floor is false may not be named as any other row's comparability.bias.floor_measurement_ref. The producing tool stamped it unusable as a zero-point -- cross-lane (BIAS-006), cross-stack, or head-substituted -- and a downstream row may not launder it by citing it.

comparability.key equals 'cmp--' + sha256(join('|', [key_inputs.panel_id, key_inputs.reference_id, key_inputs.metric_name, key_inputs.direction, key_inputs.accumulation_dtype, key_inputs.stack_relation, key_inputs.head_policy]))[:16]. Recomputed, never trusted.

key_inputs.panel_id == measurement.panel_ref; key_inputs.reference_id == measurement.reference_ref; key_inputs.metric_name == metric.name; key_inputs.direction == metric.direction; key_inputs.accumulation_dtype == estimator.accumulation_dtype; key_inputs.stack_relation == estimator.stack_relation; key_inputs.head_policy == estimator.head_policy.
Within one comparability key, all member measurements agree on measurement_scope.scored_positions, or every disagreeing member has covers_full_panel=false plus a subset_of_panel disclosure.

invariants.amended: v1.0.0: added pipeline_ref. brandonmusic's v44/v71/v75 rows measure the same weights on the same panel against the same teacher and differ only in the serving stack -- which is the variable he is actually reporting. Excluding pipeline_ref would have rejected three legitimate rows as duplicates.
invariants.statement: No two measurements share (artifact_ref, panel_ref, reference_ref, pipeline_ref, metric.name, estimator.stack_relation, estimator.head_policy, provenance.measured_by) unless one has status superseded/retracted and names the other via supersedes.
A comparability key with exactly one member is reported: a single-row group is a number nobody can compare to anything, and the README must say so rather than imply a ranking.
index.json comparability_keys is exactly the set of distinct keys present in measurements, with correct member_count, panel_id, reference_id and metric_name.

index.json comparability_keys[].comparability -- the like-for-like predicate over the secondary dimensions the seven-field key deliberately omits (measurement lane, candidate pipeline, artifact scope coverage, hardware) -- equals the predicate recomputed from the data by tools/registry_predicate.py. comparable='false' whenever a recorded secondary dimension differs across a group's live members, 'unknown' when one is unrecorded, 'true' only when all four are recorded and homogeneous. The key is a NECESSARY partition, never a sufficient certificate; this predicate is the machine-readable rest of the contract, and a hand-edited one is rejected exactly like a forged key.

determinism.identical_across_runs=true requires evidence_kind in {tokenwise_kld_sha256, logits_tensor_sha256, hidden_state_tensor_sha256, sealed_tokenwise_digest}, distinct_evidence_hash_count == 1, len(evidence_hashes) == 1, and run_count >= 2. Receipt-file and archive hashes are never acceptable evidence: report files embed run indices, paths and timestamps and differ across bit-identical runs (see the five-run K6 receipt, where report_file_sha256 differs per run while tokenwise_kld_sha256 is constant).

If determinism.run_means is present, len(run_means) == run_count, min_run_mean == min(run_means), max_run_mean == max(run_means), and population_stddev_of_run_means matches the population standard deviation of run_means to 1e-12 relative tolerance.
If metric.name is mean_of_run_means_tokenwise_kld and run_means is present, metric.value equals mean(run_means) to 1e-12 relative tolerance.

invariants.amended: v1.0.0: original wording required identical_across_runs=true whenever stddev was 0, which would have forced a false determinism claim onto every zero-spread row that publishes no per-run output digest. Inverted to match the invariant's stated intent.
invariants.statement: population_stddev_of_run_means == 0 with run_count >= 2 may NOT be presented as identical_across_runs=true unless evidence_kind is a content-hash kind (tokenwise_kld_sha256, logits_tensor_sha256, hidden_state_tensor_sha256, sealed_tokenwise_digest) with exactly one distinct hash. Equal run means alone are recorded as evidence_kind=run_mean_equality_only with identical_across_runs false or null. Equal means without a content hash is a coincidence claim, not a determinism claim.
determinism.run_count == 0 only when status=pending.
A self-measured published row with run_count < 5 carries a disclosure with code=reduced_run_count.
Every record's disclosures array is non-empty. A record with nothing to disclose carries exactly one entry with code=no_known_deviations, severity=info, affects_comparability=false.
code=no_known_deviations never coexists with any other disclosure in the same array.
A disclosure with severity=blocking forces status in {pending, retracted}: a blocking caveat and a published number are contradictory.
Disclosure codes come from the registry's known-code list; a new code requires adding it to that list in the same change, so codes stay groupable.
artifact.huggingface.revision is non-null for every artifact backing a published measurement, or the row carries a revision_unpinned disclosure with affects_comparability=true.

Two artifacts never share the same (huggingface.repository, huggingface.revision, huggingface.path) unless their scope_digest differs and both disclose why. One repository can hold several artifacts (subfolders, branches, .gguf files), which is what path distinguishes.
weights.size_gb, when present, equals weights.size_bytes / 1e9 to 1e-6 relative tolerance.
cross_refs.local_ai_registry.match_confidence=exact requires model_instance_id to be present and to satisfy the shared id pattern.
weights.size_bytes is accompanied by weights.size_basis naming which total it is. Sizes are only compared within one basis.
Two artifacts sharing (repository, revision) with no path selector are reported: if one repository really holds both, huggingface.path should say which is which.

uncertainty.method=window_block_bootstrap_bca requires bootstrap_b, bootstrap_seed, cluster_unit, interval_kind, both ci95 endpoints and clusters>=2. An interval with no stated resampling unit is not an interval.

uncertainty.se_total requires se_clustered, sigma_run and sigma_run_runs>=2, and must equal hypot(se_clustered, sigma_run) to 1e-9 relative. Publishing a combined SE without its two parts hides which one is moving.
uncertainty.sigma_run requires sigma_run_runs>=2 and must not exceed determinism.run_count. A sigma over two runs is |delta|/sqrt(2) with one degree of freedom and must be read as such.

measurement_scope.scope_name other than 'panel25' requires covers_full_panel=false and a subset_detail. A calibration-clean sub-scope mean is not the panel mean: excluding contaminated windows moves different quants in opposite directions (measured: malaiwah rows fall 12.6-16.2%, brandonmusic's 4bpw rises 1.6%).
measurement_scope.calibration_overlap_scan requires a scope_name, so the scan result is attached to the scope it produced.
by_domain entries that quote ci95 endpoints must state interval_kind, and their scored_positions must sum to measurement_scope.scored_positions.

estimator.vocab_masking_policy should be stated for every row. It is NOT a comparability key input: the measured masked-vs-unmasked difference on a real teacher window is about 1e-10 nats (+7.2e-9 relative), 83000x smaller than the tightest real uncertainty in this registry, so it cannot move a comparison. It is recorded because a protocol divergence that is negligible must still be visible.

A row carrying a protocol block should carry both hashes. Two rows are protocol-comparable when protocol.scoring_sha256 matches; a differing file_sha256 with a matching scoring hash is a provenance note, not an incomparability.

A row whose uncertainty.sigma_run is nonzero must also carry a TOTAL-uncertainty interval, either as uncertainty.ci95_total or named explicitly in uncertainty.note. The block bootstrap resamples windows WITHIN one cold run, so ci95_low/high can never contain run-to-run spread: on a nondeterministic kernel path those endpoints are the statistical half only and understate the row's own uncertainty. Every row in this registry today has sigma_run exactly 0.0 -- brandonmusic's five 4bpw runs are bitwise identical and so are ours -- so this passes vacuously and is a LATCH, not a gate: the first measurement on a nondeterministic path (his NVFP4 MoE path is the known example, sigma_run 3.3e-4) fails here until `uncertainty` gains a real ci95_total field. That schema addition is owed and is deliberately not pre-added, so that nothing claims a field it has never emitted.
Validation performs no network access. Every $ref resolves from the local schema/ directory and every source is checked for shape only, never fetched.
No module reachable from the tools imports a networking library (socket, ssl, urllib, http, requests, huggingface_hub, aiohttp). Sources are shape-checked, never fetched.
panel.sealed=true requires identity.panel_token_sha256 non-null and identity.hash_covers in {token_ids, token_manifest}.
identity.panel_receipt_sha256 is never reused as identity.panel_token_sha256, and never appears in any determinism.evidence_hashes array.
When contexts, positions_per_context and scored_positions_total are all non-null and scoring_window.windowed=false, scored_positions_total == contexts * positions_per_context.

invariants.amended: v1.0.0: restated as a family rule. Two sibling scoring-window views of one parent share the parent's digest without either deriving from the other, which the original pairwise wording rejected.
invariants.statement: Two panels never share an identity.panel_token_sha256 unless they belong to one token-identity family: a connected component of the derived_from graph in which every edge has derivation.kind in {reformat, scoring_window_change}. Those derivations re-score identical tokens; every other derivation changes which tokens are in the panel and must therefore change the digest.

A panel with derived_from and derivation.kind=scoring_window_change has a scoring_window.score_from different from its parent's. This is the check that keeps a score-from-1024 number out of the score-from-0 table.
panel.contamination.checked=false is reported for any panel backing a strict-class measurement.
A measurement with comparability.class=strict requires panels[panel_ref].sealed=true.

A panel whose derivation.kind is shard_subset or stratum_subset does NOT share its parent's identity.panel_token_sha256: it contains different tokens, so an identical digest would be a false claim of identical content.
A panel that declares derivation.kind=scoring_window_change has strictly fewer scored_positions_total than its parent, and its scoring_window.score_from is greater than the parent's.

provenance.measured_by=self-measured requires provenance.measurer.is_registry_maintainer=true AND at least one provenance.sources entry with kind in {receipt_file, hf_file, github_file} and a non-null sha256.
provenance.measured_by != self-measured requires measurer.is_registry_maintainer to be false or absent, comparability.class=advisory, and a disclosure with code=author_reported_only.
provenance.independently_verified=true requires provenance.verification.verified_by to be a DIFFERENT party than provenance.measurer (different name and different handle).
provenance.independently_verified is never true on a row whose provenance.sources contains no verifiable source (all sources of kind private_communication or url without sha256).
Every source with kind receipt_file whose uri is a local filesystem path also has a published mirror source (hf_file or github_file). A receipt only we can see is a receipt nobody can check.
The attribution.name on a producer/author/measurer of a third-party artifact or panel is never the registry maintainer. Credit is not transferable.

A row carrying an author_reported_only disclosure is never measured_by=self-measured. Relabelling somebody else's measurement as ours is the single worst thing this registry could do, so it is checked from both directions.
A measured_by=self-measured row names a pipeline whose author is the measurer. A number we claim to have produced must have run on a stack we own.

invariants.amended: v1.0.2 (audit 2026-08-29): the old gate compared measurer.handle against produced_by.repository, two strings the submitter types, so a receipt that wrote the maintainer's handle in both fields minted a strict self-measured row in the flagship comparability group.
invariants.enforced_by: tools/registry_add.py submission_to_records (exit 8, or downgrade + attribution_downgraded disclosure)
invariants.statement: An inbound submission may not be attributed to the registry maintainer on the strength of anything inside the submission. produced_by.repository must be a maintainer-owned repository AND the operator must assert the attribution at the command line (registry_add --maintainer-attribution); an unasserted maintainer claim is recorded as third-party-reported with an attribution_downgraded disclosure. self-measured is the registry's highest trust level and comparability.class=strict follows from it, so it is a property of the invocation, never of the file: no pull request and no CI job can mint it.

A measured_by=self-measured row cites at least one hashed source that the registry maintainer actually holds: a local receipt path, or a URI in the maintainer's own HuggingFace/GitHub namespace. A row whose entire evidence lives in a third party's repository is that party's measurement wearing our name -- the failure mode PROV-007 only catches while the author_reported_only disclosure is still attached.

A row generated from a submission receipt whose lane is not sealed-ep8 carries a non_sealed_lane disclosure with affects_comparability=true. submission.schema.json states that the lane forces the matching disclosure code; without this, a streaming-lane number lands in the sealed lane's comparability group with nothing on the row to say so.

A measurement whose pipeline record declares lane.name other than sealed-ep8 carries a non_sealed_lane disclosure with affects_comparability=true AND a comparability.bias block. The comparability key has seven inputs and none of them is the lane, so two rows produced on different machines by different code paths land in the same table by construction. PROV-011 forces the disclosure on the submission path only; this forces it on every path, including rows the maintainer seeds. Additionally, a lane.bridge that names a sealed_measurement_ref must name a measurement on the bridge's own panel_ref, produced by a DIFFERENT pipeline: a lane cannot be its own baseline.
Every *_ref in every record resolves to an existing record whose id matches exactly and whose collection matches the ref's id prefix.
Ids are unique within a collection and globally unique across collections.
measurement.model_ref equals artifacts[measurement.artifact_ref].model_ref.
references[measurement.reference_ref].panel_ref equals measurement.panel_ref. A teacher captured on a different panel can never back a measurement.
artifacts[references[m.reference_ref].artifact_ref].model_ref equals measurement.model_ref, unless the reference carries a disclosure with code=cross_model_reference.
panels[m.panel_ref].model_scope contains measurement.model_ref.
panels[p].tokenizer.id equals models[m].tokenizer.id for every model m in the panel's model_scope.
A panel's derived_from does not form a cycle, and the parent panel exists.
artifact.derived_from_artifact_ref does not form a cycle.

measurement.supersedes, comparability.bias.floor_measurement_ref, provenance.verification.verification_measurement_ref and reference.self_consistency.floor_measurement_ref all resolve to existing measurements, and none is self-referential.

reference.reference_kind=dequantized_from_quant requires artifacts[reference.artifact_ref].kind=dequantized, and every measurement using that reference is comparability.class=advisory with a bias.kind=dequantized_reference.
reference.reference_kind starting with native_ requires artifacts[reference.artifact_ref].kind=base.
A reference whose capture.head_source=shared_head_artifact requires every measurement against it to have estimator.head_policy=shared_reference_head, and vice versa.
reference.self_consistency.floor_measurement_ref is set for every reference backing at least one cross_stack measurement.

A submission's declared reference.teacher_receipt_sha256 must equal the capture_receipt_sha256 of the reference record it names. Where the reference record carries no capture digest the row is forced to disclose teacher_capture_unverified, which makes it advisory.

reference.reference_kind=quantized_proxy requires artifacts[reference.artifact_ref].kind in {quant,requantized}, and every measurement using that reference carries a different_reference_kind disclosure (affects_comparability) and is comparability.class=advisory. A quantized_proxy is the most-faithful PUBLISHED artifact of a family that releases no unquantized weights, DESIGNATED as the reference so its children are measurable at all; it is not a measured floor, and rows against it are systematically smaller than they would be against true unquantized weights.

A measurement produced by executing repository-shipped modeling code (trust_remote_code) carries a remote_code disclosure with affects_comparability, AND a RECORDED harness -- the executed .py files are revision-pinned and content-digested exactly like the suite's own estimator closure. Policy (approved 2026-09-01): revision-pinned, every shipped .py digested into harness.code_digests, HF token absent from the capture environment, disclosure on every resulting row. A remote_code row with an unrecorded harness is refused: 'we ran code we did not hash' is precisely the claim this registry exists to make impossible. Tightened 2026-08-31 (peer-review follow-up): a RECORDED harness alone does not corroborate the disclosure -- the row's harness.code_digests[] must contain at least one entry with role=remote_model_code, digesting the repository-shipped .py files the disclosure warns about. A harness that hashes only the suite's own closure beside a remote_code disclosure is refused: 'we hashed what ran' must be true for exactly the code that makes the row need the disclosure.
measurement.scope_digest equals the recomputed digest of artifacts[measurement.artifact_ref].scope.

artifact.scope_digest equals the canonical digest recomputed from artifact.scope: sorted 'class=treatment:format@bpw' segments joined by '|', then '|head=<head_policy>|kv=<kv_cache_dtype>'. bpw omitted (no '@') when null.

artifact.scope.policy=uniform requires all assignments with treatment=quantized to share one (format, bits_per_weight); policy=mixed requires at least two distinct (format, bits_per_weight) pairs among quantized assignments.
artifact.scope.assignments has no duplicate (tensor_class, layer_range) pair, and covers at minimum: embed_tokens, lm_head, and at least one attn.* and one mlp.*/moe.* class.
If scope.head_policy=quantized then some assignment with tensor_class=lm_head has treatment=quantized; if native, that assignment has treatment=native. The two statements of head handling must agree.
codec.bits_per_weight_effective, when present, lies between the minimum and maximum bits_per_weight over quantized assignments and 16.
measurement_scope.covers_full_panel=true requires measurement_scope.scored_positions == panels[panel_ref].structure.scored_positions_total (when that is non-null), and contexts == panel contexts.
codec.calibration.overlaps_any_panel=true requires overlapping_panel_refs to be non-empty, and every measurement of that artifact against a listed panel carries an affects_comparability disclosure.

An artifact with any scope.assignments entry whose treatment is 'unknown' carries a disclosure with code=artifact_identity_incomplete, and no measurement of that artifact is comparability.class=strict.
A submission with measurement_scope.covers_full_panel=false must carry a subset_of_panel disclosure, and may never score more positions than the panel it names.
uncertainty.ci95_low <= metric.value <= uncertainty.ci95_high whenever all three are non-null.
uncertainty.method=none requires ci95_low and ci95_high to be null; a stated interval requires a stated method.
metric.units matches metric.name: *_kld -> nats, mean_jsd -> bits or nats, top1_agreement -> fraction in [0,1], perplexity_ratio -> ratio.
A KL-family metric.value is >= -1e-9; a negative mean KL is an estimator bug, not a result.
auxiliary_metrics.top1_agreement is present on every published KL row: a KL number without top-1 agreement hides which kind of divergence it is.

invariants.amended: v1.0.1 (audit 2026-08-28): statement narrowed to what the check actually enforces. An adversarial fixture that rounded a headline value to 4 decimal places passed STAT-006 cleanly, because a rounded float round-trips through repr like any other.
invariants.statement: metric.value survives serialization without precision loss: repr(value) round-trips to the same float and the serialized line contains that repr, so the data file never stores a display-rounded number in place of the computed one. LIMIT, stated because the wording used to imply more: this cannot detect a value that was already rounded BEFORE it reached the registry -- 0.0053 round-trips perfectly. Binding a value to its receipt is the seeder's job (live-read for the Qwen rows) and, for the transcribed GLM rows, a manual fetch-and-hash against provenance.sources[].sha256.

A row whose provenance.measured_by is not self-measured does not name the registry maintainer in measurer.name, measurer.handle or measurer.url. The rendered Attribution column reads measurer.name, so a submission carrying name: <maintainer> on a throwaway handle printed as the maintainer's own measurement while every handle-keyed check stayed quiet.

A published quantized row does not report LESS divergence than the measurement floor of its own comparability group on its own lane. Unquantized weights measured through the same stack are the zero-point; a number below them is a defect, not a ranking.

When no floor was measured on a row's own lane, the row is still bounded by the floors in its comparability group on other lanes, with a 5% margin. This is a bound, not a paired comparison: BIAS-006 still forbids SUBTRACTING a cross-lane floor. The measured lane offset on this registry is 8.5e-06 nats, ~6e-04 of the floor.

A comparability group that ranks more than one published row has a measurement floor on some lane. Reported once per group: a ranked table with no zero-point has nothing bounding how low a member may be reported.

Every measurement row carries a `harness` block, and every row whose id is NOT in schema/harness-grandfather.json carries one with recorded=true and "metric.value" in covers. The grandfather list is frozen and is never appended to: a NEW row that cannot state which code produced its number is refused. Existing rows are grandfathered rather than invalidated -- their receipts are hashed and their values reproduce -- but they say so on the row (HARN-004).

harness.recorded=false requires harness_id=null and no code_digests, and harness.recorded=true requires a non-empty code_digests, a boundary, tool_versions and a repository. An unrecorded harness must never carry digests reconstructed from a later checkout: those bytes are not the bytes that produced the row, and a plausible digest set is a fabricated provenance record.

harness.harness_id equals 'harness--' + sha256(canonical_json({boundary, code_digests sorted by role, tool_versions with nulls dropped}))[:16]. Recomputed, never trusted -- the same rule as CMP-001. repository is deliberately NOT an input: a commit sha changes on a docs edit, which is exactly the churn the boundary exists to avoid.

A measurement row in schema/harness-grandfather.json carries a harness_unrecorded disclosure, UNLESS its harness records coverage of metric.value -- a grandfathered row whose headline is later re-derived by digested code is attributed, not unattributed, and saying otherwise would be as wrong as the omission. The liability has to be readable on the row itself; a consumer pulling one JSONL line does not read the schema directory.

A harness code_digest whose path exists in the current checkout with a DIFFERENT sha256 is reported: this row was produced by code that has since changed. Not an error -- that is the mechanism working, and it is the field test the block exists for -- but it is the answer to 'which rows predate which fix' and the validator says it out loud.
Every id in schema/harness-grandfather.json resolves to a measurement row. A stale allowlist entry is a hole: it would let a future row reuse a retired id and skip HARN-001.

A by_domain entry quoting ci95 endpoints over fewer than 10 windows must carry coverage_measured. Below that many clusters no bootstrap interval delivers its nominal level -- measured 81.6% for BCa and 92.3% for bootstrap-t on log(mean) at g=5-7 -- so an interval that states only '95%' is stating something that was never true of it. This is STAT-01: the defect was not that the endpoints were computed wrongly, it was that the row claimed a level nobody had measured.

Within one row, no two by_domain entries share a non-null bootstrap_seed. STAT-17: at equal window counts a shared seed gives byte-identical resample index streams across domains, so the strata share their Monte-Carlo error -- measured |r| up to 0.57 on the real panel -- and share it arbitrarily, pairing domain A's k-th window with domain B's k-th, which are unrelated windows. The published per-domain interval goes further and uses no resample stream at all, so it has no Monte-Carlo error to share; the invariant remains because domain_table can still be asked for a bootstrap interval.

A by_domain entry quoting ci95 endpoints states interval_method, and its ci95_low is >= 0. A bootstrap method additionally states bootstrap_b and bootstrap_seed; delta_t_log states df and t_critical and reports both bootstrap fields as null, because 'this interval used no resampling' is a fact about it and a missing key would read as an oversight. A negative lower bound on a KL divergence is an estimator artifact, not a result: bootstrap-t on the RAW mean produces one on 5 of this registry's 42 cells, which is why the published interval works on the log scale.

A disclosure with asserts_provenance=true carries a non-empty sources array. PROC-01: metric rows have always required a hashed receipt, but an ASSERTION about mechanism or lineage required nothing, so a prose provenance claim reached two published dataset cards and two registry rows with no source at all and passed validation. An assertion is a published claim exactly as much as a number is.

Every source cited by a provenance assertion is PINNED: a github_file or hf_file uri carrying a 40-hex commit or a revision in its path, or any source carrying a sha256. A uri naming /blob/main/ or /resolve/main/ is refused outright. Cite by COMMIT, never by branch -- line numbers move, and a citation that silently stops pointing at what it claimed is worse than no citation, because it still reads as evidence.

On an artifact or model record, a disclosure whose detail names a source-code file (.py/.sh/.c/.cc/.cpp/.cu/.h/.rs/.go, or such a name followed by a line range) must set asserts_provenance=true. Without this the marker is opt-in and PROV-014 is decorative: the failure PROC-01 describes is exactly an author writing a mechanism claim and not thinking of it as one.

No published uri field may be a host-absolute POSIX, file:, UNC, home-relative or Windows drive path. Evidence that resolves only on one maintainer's filesystem is unavailable evidence; cite an immutable public URL or a committed repository-relative path.

title: Cross-record invariants for registry_validate.py
